long_biography.plain_text:
Advertising gave Roberto Justus the platform that made him one of Brazil's most visible business figures. After leaving his father's construction company, he joined a small agency, applying administrative and financial discipline while his partner led creative work. He founded Newcomm after leaving that partnership, assembled a group of agencies and partnered it with WPP, which became controlling shareholder. A staged sale of his shares completed his exit from ownership, while television presenting extended his public profile.

Construction brought Justus back to his family's original industry by a different route. He acquired assets in light-steel-frame building, organised them into SteelCorp and became its controlling shareholder and chief executive. The group combines a factory with a construction-technology business, moving much of building production from work sites into controlled industrial facilities. It applies repeatable modular systems to housing, data centres, commercial buildings and other large projects.
